_exposure_notes: Exposure time per frame. Multiplies the photon-rate spectra of A and B and the dark-current rate.

optics._notes: radial_orders [2, 3] gives 3 + 4 = 7 Zernikes, so coefficients_m needs 7 entries.

source._notes: Positions and separation in arcsec. position_angle_deg is the direction of B relative to A. (x, y) is a reference point a fraction centre_weight of the way from A to B: 0 = A, 0.5 = midpoint, F_B/(F_A+F_B) ~ 0.24 = photocentre, which nearly decorrelates the position from the separation (scripts/reference_point_fisher.py).

spectra._notes: Photon-rate spectra: SED [photons/s/m^2/nm] x collecting area -> incident photons/s per bin; throughput is kept separate as filt_weights. n_coarse ~ 2K (K = constrainable spectral modes) propagates only n_coarse wavelengths and Hermite-interpolates the rest; null propagates all n_wavels. Here n_coarse = 2K per star with K = 16 (A), 12 (B) from scripts/constrainable_modes.py for 10 co-fit frames; recompute if the spectra, throughput or frame count change.

throughput._notes: System throughput = product of components. The simulated band is where it exceeds threshold x peak (or band_nm if given); ~2.5% of detected photons fall outside 512-647 nm and are not simulated yet.

components._notes: Two sheets of glass at 0.91 each (visual estimate, as in photon_count.md)

instrument._notes: The detector is part of the dLux instrument object graph, so instrument.model() returns the expected detector image, including deterministic detector effects and the mean dark-current contribution.

detector._notes: Deterministic transformations of the expected image. Custom layers may be implemented as dLux DetectorLayer subclasses and included directly in instrument.model(). Layers are evaluated in the order listed.

layers.name: high_frequency_jitter
layers._notes: High-frequency pointing jitter is represented by convolution of the expected image with a Gaussian kernel.

layers.name: local_pixel_scale_variation
layers._notes: The polynomial maps nominal detector coordinates to physical coordinates; its spatially varying Jacobian produces local pixel-scale variation.

layers.name: pixel_response
layers._notes: If pixel_response_map_path is null, a random Gaussian flat (1 + flat_sigma * N(0, 1)) is drawn from the run seed.

layers.name: dark_current_mean
layers._notes: Adds rate_e_per_s_per_pixel * exposure_time_s to every pixel before stochastic sampling (mean_e_per_pixel, if given, overrides this).

noise_sampling._notes: Stochastic realization applied after instrument.model() returns the expected electrons. The ordering is physically important.

miscellaneous_effects._notes: Additional scene- or optics-level effects. These are distinct from detector response and stochastic detector noise.

temporal_planetary_signal._notes: Optional time-dependent companion signal evaluated separately for each output frame.
